profile.reading:
DartPoints operates a colocation facility at 8480 Palmetto Commerce Parkway in Ladson, South Carolina, inside Palmetto Commerce Park, a large industrial and logistics park in the tri county area where Charleston, Berkeley, and Dorchester counties meet, with DartPoints' own materials placing this specific parcel in Charleston County. The facility began as Immedion, a Southeastern colocation operator that built the North Charleston area site as part of a small regional footprint, before DartPoints acquired Immedion in 2021 in a deal the company said tripled its total data center footprint to eight facilities across seven markets in Ohio, Indiana, North Carolina, and South Carolina. DartPoints itself grew out of earlier rural and secondary market fiber and colocation providers and has positioned itself as a builder of infrastructure in markets larger operators tend to skip.

DartPoints' own current specification page for this site, referenced internally as CHS01, states a 15,000 square foot data hall, 90 tons of N plus 1 redundant cooling, seven on site network providers, and two power figures worth keeping separate rather than treating as one number, 1.3 megawatts of utility power delivered to the building, and a critical IT load capacity of 100 kilowatts. That gap between utility feed and actual IT load is common in colocation facilities built with room to grow, and it means this site's IT capacity today is a small fraction of the power physically available to it. No diesel standby generator rating or onsite generation figure specific to this address was found in operator materials reviewed for this entry.

Because Palmetto Commerce Park sits at the edge of several utility territories in the Charleston area, this research could not confirm with certainty whether the parcel is served by Dominion Energy South Carolina or by Berkeley Electric Cooperative, both of which serve parts of the surrounding tri county region, and no county assessor record was pulled to confirm parcel ownership, year built, or improved square footage separate from the operator's stated data hall size. What is documented is DartPoints' 2021 acquisition of the Immedion asset, the facility's role in a wider seven market footprint, and its stated cooling and power design as published on the operator's own site. What remains undocumented locally is any zoning case, incentive agreement, or utility interconnection filing specific to this parcel, and the exact year the building was originally constructed under Immedion.
profile.capacity_note: DartPoints' own current CHS01 spec sheet separates 1.3 MW of utility power from 100 kW of critical IT load. This row's critical_it_mw was previously set to 1.3, which was the utility figure mislabeled as IT load, and has been corrected to 0.1 MW to match the operator's own labeled breakdown.
profile.research_note: Stored critical_it_mw column value of 1.3 likely mismatched: DartPoints' own current chs01 page (dartpoints.com/locations/chs01-charleston-sc/) explicitly separates "1.3 MW utility power" from "critical IT load capacity: 100 kW". Recommend the critical_it_mw column be revisited against the 100 kW figure rather than 1.3 MW, and utility_power_mw populated with 1.3 if that column is empty. Did not confirm which electric utility serves the Charleston County side of Palmetto Commerce Park versus Berkeley Electric Cooperative territory.
sources_tried: DartPoints own dedicated Charleston location page, DartPoints own NOVA Infrastructure press release, and independent Data Center Dynamics trade press coverage of the same transaction
profile.community_note: Ladson and the wider Palmetto Commerce Park corridor have become a magnet for much larger data center proposals in Berkeley County in recent years, driven by hyperscale operators, but DartPoints' Charleston facility predates that wave and operates at a scale, and in a regulatory posture, closer to a traditional regional colocation provider than to a utility scale campus. No community opposition or incentive package specific to this address was identified in this research.

reading.body:
DartPoints Charleston operates 1.3 MW of IT capacity in Ladson, South Carolina, positioning it as a modest regional facility rather than infrastructure for large-scale AI training workloads.

The facility sits within a fragmented South Carolina data center market. Four of fourteen mapped sites in the state publish capacity figures, and DartPoints Charleston ranks third among them at 1.3 MW, representing roughly 20 percent of the 6.6 MW total disclosed across those four facilities. The remaining ten sites report no public capacity data, so the true scale of South Carolina's inventory is larger than published figures reveal. This opacity is typical for regional operators serving enterprise colocation and managed services rather than hyperscale cloud.

At 1.3 MW, the compute footprint constrains workload type. Assuming 10 kW per rack for mixed enterprise loads, the campus supports roughly 130 racks. At 40 kW per rack, typical for AI training, that same capacity yields approximately 32 racks. Large-scale model training and inference typically operate at campus scales measured in tens of megawatts, not single-digit figures. The operator does not publish rack counts, power density targets, or AI-specific certifications, leaving the facility's positioning for AI work unaddressed by available data.

DartPoints Charleston is consistent with a regional colocation strategy serving Fortune 500 companies, universities, and hospital systems in Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets across the Southeast. Whether it is configured or marketed for AI workloads specifically remains unknown from published specifications alone.
